title: Compositional Econ Mapper: per-route/model/customer cost & latency attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a compositional attribution service that maps raw runtime telemetry (token counts, GPU kernel time, batch boundaries, cache hits, and span traces) into stable per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns. This service will produce deterministic, explainable line items that the Console and billing/analytics pipelines can consume. Key goals: account for shared resources (multi-tenant GPU time, batched inference), handle fallback routing and model variants, and produce both realtime (streaming) and daily rollups with bounded error guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Service emits per-request JSON with attribution fields: cpu_time_ms, gpu_time_ms, token_count, kv_cache_savings_tokens, batching_overhead_ms, model_variant_cost_units, route_id, model_id, customer_id.
Realtime stream consumer (kafka topic) receives < 100ms processing latency for steady 5k rps ingestion using current dev cluster for headroom testing.
Rollup job produces daily per-tenant summaries with error <= 2% compared to ground-truth sampling of raw GPU utilization traces for a 24h window.
Deterministic attribution for identical request traces (idempotent mapping regardless of ingestion order).
Console displays line-item breakdown and links to causal spans for debug (linkable span_id).
Automated unit + integration tests covering cache-hit vs cache-miss paths, batching boundaries, and model-fallback scenarios.
design_decisions: Use a compositional pipeline: first normalize raw telemetry into canonical events, then apply sequential attribution passes (token-level, kernel-level, batch-level). This keeps passes small and testable.
Prefer deterministic heuristics over probabilistic sampling for per-request attribution; daily rollups can use calibrated sampling to bound aggregate error.

Represent shared GPU time as a proportional apportionment by effective request weight (token count adjusted by model complexity factor) rather than naive equal split; this yields fairer per-customer economics under mixed workloads.
Keep KV cache savings as token-equivalents instead of trying to convert to GPU-ms directly in realtime — convert to cost units in rollup using measured token->ms mapping per-model.
Surface causal span links provided by the serving runtime; where absent, attach a synthesized provenance path with deterministic hashing to aid debugging.
implementation_notes: Normalization layer implemented as Flink job reading runtime telemetry topic; outputs canonical events to an intermediate topic 'telemetry.normalized.v1'.
Attribution passes implemented as lightweight kstreams microservice (java/scala) to allow sticky partitioning by route_id + model_id for deterministic ordering.

Proportional apportionment algorithm: weight_i = tokens_i * model_complexity_factor(model_id); apportioned_gpu_ms_i = gpu_ms_batch * (weight_i / sum_weights). Store model_complexity_factor in config service and refresh on model onboarding.

Batch boundary detection uses start/end timestamps + batch_id + observed kv cache hit metadata to split kernel time across requests within a batch. If batch metadata missing, fall back to token-proportional split with an alert metric tagging such occurrences.
Expose a small rewrite rule engine for special-cases (e.g., server-side tool-calls that should be charged to tenant X); rules are versioned and tied to release tags.
testing_plan: Unit tests for normalization and attribution passes covering: single-request, multi-request batch, cache-hit cascade, and fallback routing.
Integration harness that replays 48h compressed production trace into a staging cluster to validate deterministic outputs and measure 24h rollup error vs ground-truth sampling.
Load test to sustain 10k rps ingestion for realtime path; assert p95 processing latency < 100ms and p99 < 300ms.
Fault-injection tests: drop telemetry fields, reorder events, duplicate events — service must be idempotent and emit alerts for missing critical metadata.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): deploy to console-backend-canary and enable attribution for 1% of internal routes; monitor cost drift dashboards and latency SLOs for 48 hours.
Stage 2 (expanded): 10% of routes for 5 days; run replay comparison job and collect discrepancy metrics.
Stage 3 (full): enable for all routes and mark legacy aggregator read-only; keep both systems running for a 7-day parallel window before decommissioning legacy pipelines.
Emergency rollback: switch Console read path to legacy aggregator - this is fast path and requires feature-flag toggle in console config.
